messages:
sophie: Heads-up: Java onboarding sampleapp (okhttp) is returning mixed embedding lengths in the same /embeddings response during rerank flows. Looks correlated with auth refresh + HTTP/2 multiplexing.
yusuf: which model and dims? can you share repro?
sophie: model=redwood-embed-1 (expected 512). Repro: batch 12 items -> expire token mid-flight -> SDK refresh + retry. Intermittently response contains a couple of 256-length embeddings while others are 512. Downstream reranker chokes.
emma: raw dims-only snippet: {"data": [{"id":0,"len":512},{"id":1,"len":256},{"id":2,"len":512}], "model": "redwood-embed-1"}
This is different from the axios/urllib3 keepalive cases we've seen. OkHttp using HTTP/2 multiplexing may interleave frames at transport layer.
yusuf: interesting. Java SDK parity gap: node/python already have embedding shape guards, but java-sdk doesn't. That would silently deliver garbage.
sophie: yep. Root cause seems to be: when token expires, client cancels the call; transport keeps the HTTP/2 stream open or reuses stream IDs and our response collector merges frames from prior stream into new parse buffer.
emma: short-term mitigations: 1) add strict embedding length validation in java-sdk and throw EmbeddingShapeException when mismatch found. 2) set okhttp newCall().cancel(); and create a fresh ConnectionSpec / force a new stream on retry (disable HTTP/2 multiplexing for retried requests). 3) add telemetry event "mixed_embedding_dim_java".
yusuf: agree. Also update batching helper to reset parser state between attempts. We'll mirror shape-guard implementations from node/python to keep parity.
sophie: I'll open java-sdk#121 with shape checks + unit tests and add an e2e that simulates 401 mid-stream by returning 401 after first chunk.
relay-bot: ticket created: RT-10444 runtime: validate embedding lengths per response and return diagnostic 5xx when inconsistent.
emma: server-side guard would help: if the runtime reads inconsistent lengths within a single response body it should fail the request with a clear error rather than handing out mixed vectors. Add model name and expected dim to the error for easier debugging.
yusuf: also consider a response metadata header like X-Embedding-Dim so clients can validate header before parsing heavy arrays. Might help low-level clients that don't fully parse JSON before allocating.
sophie: quick local test results: before patch, 100 iterations forced expiry -> 6 mixed-dim responses that passed silently; after adding shape guard + forcing new OkHttp stream on retry -> shape guard threw 6 errors and no polluted vectors delivered to the app. With both shape guard + disable-multiplexing on retry -> 0 occurrences.
iemma: docs: add onboarding troubleshooting note pointing to java-sdk >=0.10.2 and mention "if you see inconsistent embedding sizes, upgrade SDK and check auth/retry config".
ci-bot: CI queued for java-sdk/shape-guard (#121) :gear: job 12345
yusuf: follow-ups: 1) merge java-sdk patch 2) runtime RT-10444 3) docs blurb 4) add Java e2e in sampleapp to simulate 401 mid-stream. Assign owners and we'll close after green CI.
sophie: filing the small repro script in #devex and will paste logs. thanks all.
